title: Polymorphism: one call, many devices
tasks: DoorLock: locked by default, with lock and unlock actions
Thermostat: target, current and heating, with a dead band so it never flickers
Register both in FACTORIES and rebuild devices (no other function should need to change)
broadcast(items, action, value): try an action on every device and report who did it and who refused
explanation: snapshot() and command() were written for lights and now serve a lock and a thermostat without a single edit: that is polymorphism paying off. broadcast() relies on the contract (UnsupportedAction means 'not my kind of action') and lets everything else, such as a bad value, propagate. The thermostat's dead band is a tiny state machine: heating only changes at the two thresholds.

hints.title: DoorLock
hints.content: super().__init__(spec), then self.locked = True. state() returns {"locked": self.locked}. execute() sets self.locked = True for "lock", False for "unlock", else raises UnsupportedAction.

hints.title: Thermostat logic
hints.content: In measure(): self.current = _number(temperature, "temperature"); if self.current <= self.target - 0.5: self.heating = True; elif self.current >= self.target: self.heating = False. In set_target(): validate with 10 <= number <= 30 first, then assign self.target, then call self.measure(self.current).

hints.title: Registering and broadcasting
hints.content: FACTORIES.update({Kind.LOCK: DoorLock, Kind.THERMOSTAT: Thermostat}) then devices = build_devices(CATALOG). In broadcast(): for each device, try: device.execute(action, value) / except UnsupportedAction: skipped.append(device.id) / else: done.append(device.id).

checks.prompt: A new `Blinds` class is added next month. Which of these functions has to change so it works with the blinds?

options: None of them: only FACTORIES gets a new entry

checks.explanation: All three only use the contract (`describe()`, `execute()`), so they are closed for modification and open for extension. If they had an `isinstance` ladder, each would need editing.

checks.prompt: Why does `broadcast()` catch `UnsupportedAction` but let a `ValueError` for `dim 999` escape?

options: ValueError cannot be caught in a loop
An unsupported action is a normal fact about a device; a bad value is a mistake the caller should hear about
Python only allows one except clause

checks.explanation: Catch the narrowest exception that describes a situation you *expect*. Silently skipping a bad value would hide a bug; skipping a device that doesn't speak the action is the whole point of broadcasting.
